claims.title: Columbus reaches Cuba
claims.summary: On his first voyage Christopher Columbus anchors off the northern coast of Cuba and claims the island for Spain, his first encounter with the Taino there.

sources.label: Cuba: A Country Study
sources.publisher: Library of Congress, Federal Research Division

claims.title: Spanish conquest begins
claims.summary: Diego Velazquez leads the conquest of Cuba, founding Baracoa as the first Spanish settlement; further towns follow within a few years.

sources.label: Cuba: A Country Study
sources.publisher: Library of Congress, Federal Research Division

claims.title: Collapse of the Taino
claims.summary: Forced labour, starvation, and Old World disease all but extinguish the indigenous Taino, prompting the import of enslaved Africans.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Cuba: From the Taino and the fortified key to the Indies to a sugar colony, a contested republic, and a socialist revolution at the edge of the Cold War.", terralore.co/country/CUB/chronicle#ev-1520-collapse-of-the-taino, claim TL:CUB:event:1520:collapse-of-the-taino, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Founding of Havana
claims.summary: The Spanish found Havana, whose harbour becomes an obligatory stop on the route to the New World and the most heavily fortified port of the Caribbean.

sources.label: Old Havana and its Fortification System

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Cuba: From the Taino and the fortified key to the Indies to a sugar colony, a contested republic, and a socialist revolution at the edge of the Cold War.", terralore.co/country/CUB/chronicle#ev-1519-founding-of-havana, claim TL:CUB:event:1519:founding-of-havana, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The fortifications of Havana
claims.summary: Construction of the Castillo de la Real Fuerza and, later, the Morro and La Cabana fortresses makes Havana the fortified key to the Indies.

sources.label: Old Havana and its Fortification System

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Cuba: From the Taino and the fortified key to the Indies to a sugar colony, a contested republic, and a socialist revolution at the edge of the Cold War.", terralore.co/country/CUB/chronicle#ev-1558-the-fortifications-of-havana, claim TL:CUB:event:1558:the-fortifications-of-havana, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Sugar-and-slavery boom
claims.summary: Cuba becomes the world's leading sugar producer, importing over 600,000 enslaved Africans; by 1860 it makes nearly a third of the world's sugar.

sources.label: Cuba: Sugarcane and the growth of slavery

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Cuba: From the Taino and the fortified key to the Indies to a sugar colony, a contested republic, and a socialist revolution at the edge of the Cold War.", terralore.co/country/CUB/chronicle#ev-1820-sugar-and-slavery-boom, claim TL:CUB:event:1820:sugar-and-slavery-boom, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Grito de Yara
claims.summary: Carlos Manuel de Cespedes frees his slaves and proclaims independence at La Demajagua, beginning the Ten Years' War against Spain.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Cuba: From the Taino and the fortified key to the Indies to a sugar colony, a contested republic, and a socialist revolution at the edge of the Cold War.", terralore.co/country/CUB/chronicle#ev-1868-grito-de-yara, claim TL:CUB:event:1868:grito-de-yara, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Marti's War of Independence
claims.summary: Jose Marti orders the resumption of war and lands in Cuba, dying at Dos Rios on 19 May; the rising continues under Gomez and Maceo.

sources.label: Jose Marti — The World of 1898: The Spanish-American War

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Cuba: From the Taino and the fortified key to the Indies to a sugar colony, a contested republic, and a socialist revolution at the edge of the Cold War.", terralore.co/country/CUB/chronicle#ev-1895-marti-s-war-of-independence, claim TL:CUB:event:1895:marti-s-war-of-independence, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Sinking of the USS Maine
claims.summary: The U.S. battleship Maine explodes in Havana harbour, propelling the United States toward war with Spain over Cuba.

sources.label: The Spanish-American War, 1898
sources.publisher: U.S. Department of State, Office of the Historian

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Cuba: From the Taino and the fortified key to the Indies to a sugar colony, a contested republic, and a socialist revolution at the edge of the Cold War.", terralore.co/country/CUB/chronicle#ev-1898-sinking-of-the-uss-maine, claim TL:CUB:event:1898:sinking-of-the-uss-maine, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Spanish-American War ends Spanish rule
claims.summary: After Spain's defeat, the Treaty of Paris ends Spanish dominion over Cuba; the Teller Amendment had disclaimed U.S. annexation.

sources.label: The Spanish-American War, 1898
sources.publisher: U.S. Department of State, Office of the Historian

claims.title: The Platt Amendment
claims.summary: The U.S. Congress conditions withdrawal on the Platt Amendment, reserving a right of intervention and a naval base at Guantanamo Bay; Cuba writes it into its constitution.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Cuba: From the Taino and the fortified key to the Indies to a sugar colony, a contested republic, and a socialist revolution at the edge of the Cold War.", terralore.co/country/CUB/chronicle#ev-1901-the-platt-amendment, claim TL:CUB:event:1901:the-platt-amendment, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Republic of Cuba proclaimed
claims.summary: The United States ends its occupation and the Republic of Cuba is installed under Tomas Estrada Palma, its first president.

sources.label: A Guide to the United States' History of Recognition, Diplomatic, and Consular Relations, by Country: Cuba
sources.publisher: U.S. Department of State, Office of the Historian

claims.title: Fall of Machado
claims.summary: Amid depression and unrest the army forces dictator Gerardo Machado to flee, opening the era of Fulgencio Batista.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Cuba: From the Taino and the fortified key to the Indies to a sugar colony, a contested republic, and a socialist revolution at the edge of the Cold War.", terralore.co/country/CUB/chronicle#ev-1933-fall-of-machado, claim TL:CUB:event:1933:fall-of-machado, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Batista's coup
claims.summary: Anticipating electoral defeat, Fulgencio Batista seizes power in a bloodless coup and rules as dictator, provoking armed opposition.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Cuba: From the Taino and the fortified key to the Indies to a sugar colony, a contested republic, and a socialist revolution at the edge of the Cold War.", terralore.co/country/CUB/chronicle#ev-1952-batista-s-coup, claim TL:CUB:event:1952:batista-s-coup, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Triumph of the Revolution
claims.summary: Batista flees and the 26th of July Movement takes power; Fidel Castro soon leads the new government, which turns toward socialism.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Cuba: From the Taino and the fortified key to the Indies to a sugar colony, a contested republic, and a socialist revolution at the edge of the Cold War.", terralore.co/country/CUB/chronicle#ev-1959-triumph-of-the-revolution, claim TL:CUB:event:1959:triumph-of-the-revolution, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Bay of Pigs invasion
claims.summary: A brigade of U.S.-backed Cuban exiles lands at the Bay of Pigs in an attempt to overthrow Castro and is defeated within days.

sources.label: The Bay of Pigs Invasion and its Aftermath, April 1961-October 1962
sources.publisher: U.S. Department of State, Office of the Historian

claims.title: U.S. embargo made comprehensive
claims.summary: President Kennedy expands the trade embargo to cover nearly all commerce with Cuba and makes it permanent.

sources.label: The Bay of Pigs Invasion and its Aftermath, April 1961-October 1962
sources.publisher: U.S. Department of State, Office of the Historian

claims.title: Cuban Missile Crisis
claims.summary: Soviet nuclear missiles in Cuba trigger a thirteen-day confrontation; a U.S. quarantine and a Soviet agreement to withdraw the missiles avert nuclear war.

sources.label: The Cuban Missile Crisis, October 1962
sources.publisher: U.S. Department of State, Office of the Historian

claims.title: The Special Period begins
claims.summary: The Soviet collapse ends Cuba's subsidies and trade; Castro declares a special period of rationing and austerity as GDP contracts sharply.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Cuba: From the Taino and the fortified key to the Indies to a sugar colony, a contested republic, and a socialist revolution at the edge of the Cold War.", terralore.co/country/CUB/chronicle#ev-1991-the-special-period-begins, claim TL:CUB:event:1991:the-special-period-begins, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Raul Castro assumes the presidency
claims.summary: An ailing Fidel Castro hands power to his brother Raul, who introduces gradual economic reforms.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Cuba: From the Taino and the fortified key to the Indies to a sugar colony, a contested republic, and a socialist revolution at the edge of the Cold War.", terralore.co/country/CUB/chronicle#ev-2008-raul-castro-assumes-the-presidency, claim TL:CUB:event:2008:raul-castro-assumes-the-presidency, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Thaw with the United States
claims.summary: Obama and Raul Castro announce normalisation; diplomatic relations are restored and embassies reopen in 2015, though the embargo remains.

sources.label: Re-Establishment of Diplomatic Relations With Cuba

claims.summary: Miguel Diaz-Canel becomes president in 2018 and Communist Party leader in 2021, the first non-Castro to hold the top posts since 1959.
